name: LCRS B002018.8-415015 (Hubble)
blurb: LCRS B002018.8-415015, a post-starburst (E+A) galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: gal002247413337-hubble
story: Post-starburst galaxies like this one are among the best candidates for galaxies in transition, turning from gas-rich and star-forming to gas-poor and passively evolving through galaxy mergers. In this one, Hubble's view shows merger signatures, dust lanes across its bulge and a crop of compact star clusters likely formed in the starburst.

claims.text: The target position (00 22 47, -41 33 37) is the E+A galaxy LCRS B002018.8-415015 (EA18)
Post-starburst (E+A) galaxies are the best candidates for galaxies in transition from gas-rich and star-forming to gas-poor and passively evolving, via galaxy mergers
The E+A galaxies EA06 to EA21 of the Zabludoff et al. (1996) Las Campanas Redshift Survey sample were imaged with Hubble's ACS
Dust lanes mask a large portion of EA18's bulge
EA18 has an excess of compact point sources interpreted as star clusters formed during the starburst
